data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 proposes analyzing reasoning traces on checklist-vs-intuition conflict cases to distinguish understanding from rote adherence, but this diagnostic is circular for the non-expert panel setting. Non-experts by definition lack deep domain knowledge; their 'reasoning traces' will inevitably parrot checklist language because that is their only tool. A non-expert who gives a sophisticated causal justification on a conflict case is either reciting checklist rationale or guessing—there is no independent ground to confirm the reasoning reflects genuine structural understanding rather than post-hoc confabulation aligned with the checklist. SRC_002's own disanalogy admits non-experts 'may lack the vocabulary to articulate causal understanding even if they have it,' which undermines the trace's diagnostic value: absence of deep justification is expected and uninformative, while presence of it is suspicious rather than probative. The method cannot cleanly separate competence from compliance in the population it is designed to evaluate.
